content.title: About
content.content: Pompano (Pampus argenteus) is a marine fish from the jack family, native to warm coastal waters of the Indo‑Pacific region. Grilled fillet offers a delicate, slightly sweet flavor, firm yet tender texture, and a subtle smoky aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pompano is often called the “golden sea perch” because of its golden‑hued flesh.
The species can change sex during its life; young males may become females later on.
In China, pompano is considered a delicacy and frequently appears on upscale restaurant menus.
It grows quickly, reaching up to 60 cm and 2 kg within a year.
Pompano is commonly farmed in aquaculture, reducing pressure on wild stocks.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support heart health, reduce inflammation, and aid brain function.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Easily digestible fish protein helps build and repair muscle tissue.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D is essential for bone health, immune function, and calcium regulation.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as a powerful antioxidant and supports thyroid health.

items.title: Low mercury levels
items.content: Compared with larger predatory fish, pompano has low mercury, making it safe for regular consumption.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including pompano.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: Like any marine fish, pompano can contain trace pollutants (e.g., PCBs); purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: When grilled with added salt, sodium levels can rise; people with hypertension should monitor salt intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve grilled pompano fillet hot, drizzled with lemon juice or an olive‑oil‑based sauce. It pairs well with vegetable sides, quinoa, rice, or fresh green salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked fillet in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a bag at –18 °C; thaw in the fridge before serving.
